portName: Mykonos New Port (Tourlos) and Old Port tender pier
seoTitle: Mykonos cruise port guide: Tourlos, Sea Bus, Delos
seoDescription: Mykonos cruise port: dock at Tourlos 3 km from town or tender to the Old Port. Sea Bus €2.50 (2026), 10–12 min. Delos boat €20 plus €20 entry. Greek fee up to €20.
quickAnswer: Ships either dock at the New Port in Tourlos, about 2.5–3 km north of Mykonos Town, or anchor and tender straight to the Old Port on the edge of town. From Tourlos, the Sea Bus water taxi runs about every 30 minutes to the Old Port in 10–12 minutes for €2.50 one way (2026), and many lines also run a shuttle. Be back at the Sea Bus or tender pier 90 minutes before all-aboard.
intro: Mykonos is a small, compact port day once you reach town. The question is only how you arrive: ships that dock at Tourlos are a short boat ride or bus ride from Chora, while ships at anchor tender passengers right into the Old Port. Chora itself is a maze of whitewashed lanes that takes a morning to wander, with Little Venice and the windmills at its southern edge. The other big draw is Delos, the sacred island and archaeological site 30–40 minutes away by boat, which fits into a port day if you take an early departure. Taxis are scarce, so plan around the Sea Bus and the KTEL buses.
tenderNotes: Mykonos is both. Some ships dock at the cruise berths in the New Port (Tourlos); others anchor offshore and tender passengers to the Old Port on the northern edge of Mykonos Town, a 5–10 minute walk from the centre; the tender berths are by the Archaeological Museum (four were added in 2024, Cruise Hive). Which applies is set per call by the port authority and is printed in your daily programme. A new tender pier at the Old Port, built to take four tenders at once, was being brought into use in 2026 (CruiseMapper, May 2026); treat it as service expected to start rather than guaranteed. On days with several ships, expect tender waits of 20–45 minutes in the morning. Unlike Santorini, Mykonos has no daily cap on cruise passengers, only its berth allocation (Greek Trip Planner, October 2026); it took 762 ship calls in 2025.

terminals.name: New Port (Tourlos) cruise berths
terminals.notes: North of town, shared with ferries. Sea Bus pier a few minutes' walk from the berth. KTEL buses and any cruise-line shuttles leave from the port area. Few toilets and little shade when several ships are in.

terminals.name: Old Port tender pier
terminals.notes: On the northern edge of Mykonos Town by the old harbour. Tenders land here; the Sea Bus from Tourlos also arrives here. The Old Port KTEL bus station is nearby.

walkability.detail: From Tourlos to town is 30–40 minutes on a busy coastal road with no pavement in places and little shade. It is flat but not pleasant; take the Sea Bus or a bus. From the Old Port tender pier, everything in town (Little Venice, the windmills, Paraportiani) is within 10–15 minutes on foot, on mostly level but narrow lanes.

transportSections.detail: Small water-taxi boats leave from beside the New Port, about every 30 minutes in season, and land at the Old Port near the town hall. Buy tickets at the kiosk on the pier. In strong north winds (meltemi) the boats may stop running; use the bus instead.

transportSections.cost: Often free; some lines charge – check your daily programme
transportSections.detail: Many lines run shuttles every 15–30 minutes from Tourlos to the edge of town near the bus stations. Note the last return time.

transportSections.time: About 10 min to Fabrika; about 20 min to Old Port
transportSections.detail: Buses link Tourlos with Fabrika station (south side of town, beach buses) every 30–60 minutes and with the Old Port station about hourly. Buy tickets at the station kiosk or from the driver in cash. Timetables change each year.
There is a rank at the New Port, but Mykonos has only a few dozen taxis and waits are long when ships and ferries arrive together. Not a reliable way back to the ship.

returnTiming.rule: Be at the Old Port Sea Bus pier (or tender pier) by 16:00 for a 17:30 all-aboard.
returnTiming.detail: The Sea Bus runs about every 30 minutes and takes 10–12 minutes, so a 16:00 start allows for a full boat and one missed departure. If you are tendering, the last tender usually leaves 30 minutes before all-aboard and the afternoon queue can take 30 minutes or more. From Delos, take the 13:30 boat at the latest; the last afternoon return (15:00) leaves little margin.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: If the Sea Bus is full or not running, take the KTEL bus from the Old Port station to the New Port (about 20 minutes) or walk 35–40 minutes along the coast road. Call the ship's port agent (number in the daily programme) if you will be late.

diyVsExcursion.ship: Guided walk; price varies by line
diyVsExcursion.diy: Free on foot after a €2.50 Sea Bus (2026)
diyVsExcursion.saving: Depends on your line's tour price

diyVsExcursion.ship: Beach transfer; price varies by line
diyVsExcursion.saving: Depends on your line's tour price

excursionAdvice: Mykonos is easy to do on your own. The only case for a ship tour is Delos when the public boat schedule does not fit your call, or when meltemi winds make independent boats unreliable; ship tours have a guide on the site, which has little shade or explanation. For the town and the beaches, the Sea Bus and the KTEL buses are enough.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes docking at Tourlos at 08:00 and a Tuesday–Sunday Delos boat schedule.

steps.what: Walk to the Sea Bus pier and ride to the Old Port.
Buy Delos boat tickets at the kiosk outside the boats by the Old Port (sold from 15 minutes before departure).
Boat to Delos (30–40 minutes). Take water, a hat and sun cream; there is little shade on the site.
Explore Delos: the Terrace of the Lions, the theatre quarter and the museum.
Lunch in Chora, then walk to Little Venice and the Kato Mili windmills.
Visit Panagia Paraportiani and the lanes around Matoyianni Street.
Sea Bus back to Tourlos and be on board by 16:30, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Delos
sights.why: The mythical birthplace of Apollo and one of the largest archaeological sites in Greece, covering a whole island. Temples, houses with mosaics and the Terrace of the Lions.
sights.tip: On Mondays boats run less often (10:00 out, 13:30 back). Sailings are cancelled in strong winds.

sights.name: Little Venice
sights.why: A row of 18th-century captains' houses with balconies built over the sea on the west side of town.
sights.tip: Go in the morning. It is packed at sunset.

sights.name: Kato Mili windmills
sights.why: A row of whitewashed windmills on the low ridge above Little Venice, the island's best-known view.
sights.tip: Five minutes' walk from Little Venice. Little shade.

sights.name: Panagia Paraportiani
sights.why: A cluster of five chapels joined into one whitewashed building near the old harbour, dating from the 15th to 17th centuries.
sights.tip: Close to the Old Port, so a good first or last stop.

sights.name: Chora lanes and Matoyianni Street
sights.why: The main shopping lane and the maze of narrow streets around it, built to confuse pirates and wind.
sights.tip: Lanes are narrow and fill with tour groups from mid-morning. Note landmarks so you can find your way back.

sights.name: Archaeological Museum of Mykonos
sights.why: Pottery and grave finds from the purification pit of Rheneia, near the Old Port.
sights.tip: In 2026 open 09:00–16:00 every day except Tuesday from April to October, and 08:30–15:30 from November. Last admission is 20 minutes before closing.

sights.name: Old harbour waterfront
sights.why: The curved harbour front with the small church of Agios Nikolaos, fishing boats and the Delos ticket kiosks.
sights.tip: This is where the Sea Bus and tenders land; easy to combine with Paraportiani.

beaches.name: Agios Stefanos
beaches.howToGetThere: KTEL bus from the Old Port station, or walk 15–20 minutes north from Tourlos
beaches.note: The closest sandy beach to the New Port. Sunbeds and tavernas.

beaches.name: Ornos
beaches.note: Sheltered sandy bay, good in north winds. Buses every 30 minutes.

beaches.name: Platis Gialos
beaches.note: Family beach with sunbeds. Buses roughly hourly.

beaches.name: Paradise
beaches.note: Known for beach bars and music. Buses every 30–60 minutes.

food.dish: Kopanisti (peppery soft cheese) and louza (cured pork)
food.where: Tavernas in Chora; both are local specialities on most traditional menus
Kounelas fish taverna, near the Old Port in Chora
Niko's Taverna, near the old harbour in Chora
Bakeries and sweet shops in Chora's lanes

commonMistakes.mistake: Walking from Tourlos to town on the main road
commonMistakes.fix: Take the Sea Bus or the bus. The road is busy and has no pavement in places.

commonMistakes.mistake: Turning up for Delos on a Monday expecting the full schedule
commonMistakes.fix: Monday has fewer boats. Check the kiosk times the day before or take the 10:00 sailing.

commonMistakes.mistake: Relying on a taxi to get back to the ship
commonMistakes.fix: Mykonos has only a few dozen taxis. Use the Sea Bus or the bus and leave a buffer.

commonMistakes.mistake: Staying in Little Venice for sunset on a short call
commonMistakes.fix: Check all-aboard first. If you sail before sunset, see Little Venice in the morning.
Mykonos has the highest rate: up to €20 per passenger from June to September and €12 in October (2026), charged by your line.

safety: Mykonos Town is safe by day. The main risks are traffic on the narrow roads outside town (many have no pavement and quad bikes are common), sunburn and heat on Delos, and pickpocketing in crowded lanes and on full buses. Strong meltemi winds in July and August can stop the Sea Bus and Delos boats and make tender transfers rough.
scams: Waterfront and Little Venice restaurants that serve seafood priced by weight without showing the weight or price. Ask for the price per kilo and the weight before it is cooked.
Unlicensed drivers at the New Port offering rides into town at high flat rates. Use the Sea Bus, the bus or a marked taxi.
Bars and restaurants adding a large service charge or charging for items you did not order. Check the bill against the menu.
accessibility: If your ship docks at Tourlos, the Sea Bus is described as wheelchair accessible, and the Old Port waterfront is flat. Chora's lanes are narrow, uneven and partly stepped; Little Venice and the windmills are reachable on level-to-gentle routes from the Old Port, but expect cobbles. Tendering requires stepping into a moving boat and depends on the crew's decision on the day. Delos has rough paths and no step-free routes.
rainyDay: Rain is rare from May to September. Wind is the more common problem: in strong meltemi the Delos boats and the Sea Bus may be suspended. On a bad day, use the bus into town, visit the Archaeological Museum near the Old Port, and spend the time in Chora's cafés and shops.
crowdTips: Mykonos can have several ships and ferries in on the same day. The Old Port and Matoyianni Street are busiest from 10:00 to 13:00; Little Venice is busiest at sunset. The early Delos boats are the calmest. Go to the windmills before 10:00 or after 15:00. If you are docked, take an early Sea Bus before the shuttle queues form.

faqs.a: Sometimes. Some ships dock at the New Port in Tourlos; others anchor and tender passengers to the Old Port in town. Your daily programme says which.

faqs.q: How do I get from Mykonos cruise port to Mykonos Town?
faqs.a: From Tourlos take the Sea Bus (€2.50 in 2026, 10–12 minutes, about every 30 minutes), a cruise shuttle if offered, or the KTEL bus. Tenders land directly in town.

faqs.q: Is Mykonos walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: From the Old Port, yes. From Tourlos it is 30–40 minutes on a busy road without pavement in places, so the Sea Bus is better.

faqs.q: Can I visit Delos from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Yes. Boats leave the old harbour at 09:00, 10:00 and 11:30 (Tuesday–Sunday) for €20 return, plus €20 site entry. Return by the 12:00 or 13:30 boat on a normal call.

faqs.q: What can I do in Mykonos in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Delos in the morning, then Chora, Little Venice and the windmills in the afternoon. Or skip Delos and take a bus to Ornos or Platis Gialos beach.
Agios Stefanos is closest to Tourlos. Ornos, Platis Gialos and Paradise are 5–15 minutes by bus from Fabrika station.

faqs.q: What is the Greek cruise passenger fee for Mykonos?
faqs.a: €20 per disembarking passenger from June to September, €12 in April, May and October and €4 from November to March. It is charged by your cruise line.
Yes. Watch for traffic on roads without pavements, pickpockets in crowds and bills with unexpected charges.
